hook: Photodiode homodyne readout could detect atom-qubit states above 99% fidelity in 100 microseconds
summary: The authors propose reading out neutral-atom qubits by mixing the atoms' fluorescence with a reference beam on photodiodes, avoiding slow cameras. An analytic model of atomic motion, checked with 3D Monte Carlo simulation, finds an optimal detection time and predicts fidelity above 99% within 100 microseconds. This is simulation only, with no experiment yet.
title: Coherent Optical Readout of Neutral-Atom Qubits via Homodyne Detection of Resonant Fluorescence
